newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise gains on Italian oilfield report.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise gains on Italian oilfield report.

text.p: Shares in Enterprise Oil Plc shot higher in early trading on Monday after a report in the Financial Times said the company would shortly start full-scale development of its Italian oilfield.

Rebounding from recent weakness, the stock was up 14-1/2p at 652p by 0900 GMT. Enterprise rose to a record 697-3/4 on January 31 but has since retreated, with analysts at Merrill Lynch arguing the stock was overvalued and cutting it to "reduce".
The FT said technical breakthroughs would help the company reduce the risk of wells running dry in the field, one of western Europe's largest oilfields.
Analysts said news of the drilling breakthrough meant Enterprise was tackling the complex rock formations and the heavy type of oil in the region that had made drilling problematic.

"At one stage there was a possibility that the field would be non-commercial," said Elizabeth Butler, analyst at Panmure Gordon. "Now you could be looking at doubling the amount of recoverable reserves."
Lasmo Plc, also active in the region, was up 2-1/2p at 238.
A flow of positive news on the Italian discovery has powered Enterprise shares higher in recent months.
Simon Oddie, the company's general manager in Rome, said last month that the field would go into production later this year after "excellent" results from an appraisal drilling.
